slides.title: why a calendar beats *reacting*
slides.body: Reactive releases almost always arrive late. A calendar means data, photos and spokespeople are ready **before** journalists start looking.

slides.title: Q1 · jan–mar
items: Chinese New Year (6–7 Feb 2027): stories on SME festive demand
Ramadan & Hari Raya (est. Feb–Mar 2027): prepare releases well ahead
Annual results & 2027 targets: release your 2026 milestones

slides.title: Q2 · apr–jun
items: Mid-year: customer data or internal research
Launch new product lines ahead of mid-year sales

slides.title: Q3 · jul–sep
items: DOSM's MSME release (late July): comment with your own data
31 Aug Merdeka & 16 Sep Malaysia Day: community programmes, not just discounts

slides.title: Q4 · oct–dec
items: Budget 2028 tabling (Oct): react with SME-relevant commentary
Deepavali, 11.11 & 12.12: release promos before peak days

slides.title: the *T-14 to T+3* rule
slides.body: A working timeline for every moment:
slides.ex: T-14 research & data · T-7 final release + photos · T-3 pitch journalists · Day 0 publish & share · T+3 coverage recap

captions_meta.li_hook:
The brands that appear in the news around big moments usually prepared their releases weeks before.
Here is a 2027 PR calendar framework for Malaysia.
li_body: Recurring data releases are underrated news hooks. DOSM's MSME report, which put MSMEs at 39.7% of GDP in 2025, lands every year. A reaction release with your own numbers on publication day is an easy win.
li_points: Q1: Chinese New Year, Ramadan and Hari Raya (2027 dates are estimates), plus your annual milestones.
Q2: mid-year data, hiring and expansion, and product launches ahead of mid-year sales.
Q3: DOSM's MSME release in late July, then Merdeka and Malaysia Day with community programmes.
Q4: Budget 2028 commentary, Deepavali, 11.11 and 12.12. Send promo releases before peak days.
For every moment: T-14 research, T-7 final release, T-3 pitch, Day 0 publish, T+3 recap.
